VERDICT: CLEAN

BOUNDARY: Verified that every neighbourhood of 0 contains an open interval `(-δ,δ)` for some `δ>0` (standard topology). For `n > 1/δ`, `1/n < δ`, so `I_n = (1/(n+1),1/n) ⊆ (0,δ) ⊆ (-δ,δ)`, thus every neighbourhood meets infinitely many members; hence not locally finite at 0. Points inside any `I_n` belong to exactly one member, points elsewhere belong to none — point-finite holds. No counterexample or edge-case failure found.

SOURCES: Inspected the full text of both cited items: `def-cover-refinement-and-local-finiteness` (definitions of locally finite, point-finite, and the remark that the converse can fail) and `def-interval` (bounded open intervals are valid). The Wikipedia reference listed in the target’s sources was not load‑bearing; no claim depends on it.

CHECKED: Title, public claim (“point‑finite need not mean locally finite …”), the entire body text, and the concluding remark were read. No numbered steps or separate Remarks section exist.
